title: Post-Silicon Validation: Opportunities, Challenges and Recent Advances
snippet: Post-silicon research has developed reconfigurable debug fabrics, scan/trace combinations, restoration and visibility metrics, processor-specific recorders, and formal localization procedures~\cite{abramovici06,rootselaar99,caty05,overview,ga24,sanjaya24}. These contributions solve different observation problems. A set optimized for restoring internal state, propagating errors, detecting bit flips, or reconstructing a protocol is not automatically a certificate that every pair of classes in a declared task remains distinguishable after samples disappear. We study that narrower universal-separation question and do not claim a replacement for physical debug architectures or processor-localization systems.
ledger_relevance: Historical survey of post-silicon validation challenges, observability limits, and the distinction from pre-silicon verification and manufacturing test.
ledger_delta_or_limit: Background only; it motivates observability challenges but is not a source for the certificate theorem.

title: {IFRA}: Instruction Footprint Recording and Analysis for Post-Silicon Bug Localization in Processors
snippet: Execution-specific methods include IFRA and BLoG~\cite{ifra08,ifra09,blog10}, QED/S-QED/E-QED~\cite{qed10,qedtcad14,sqed,eqed}, protocol and memory-consistency localization~\cite{cao17,memory15}, and trace reconstruction or inconsistent-execution diagnosis~\cite{backspace,deorio11}. Their hardware grounding is stronger than our single UART simulation bridge; their outputs are not the tap-labelled $(d+1)^2$ obstruction or its projection theorem. ledger_delta_or_limit: Provides stronger processor, execution, or protocol grounding; it does not supply the tap-labelled bounded-row-loss frontier certificate or per-pair projection theorem claimed here.

title: Diagnosability of Discrete-Event Systems
section: Diagnosability with partial or unreliable observation
snippet: \subsection{Diagnosability with partial or unreliable observation} Classical discrete-event-system diagnosability asks whether faults can eventually be inferred from partial observations and provides polynomial verification constructions and stochastic extensions~\cite{sampath95,jiang01,yoo02,thorsley05,zaytoon13}. More recent work models unreliable sensors with temporal assumptions, and hybrid-barrier certificates address continuous-state cyber-physical diagnosis~\cite{dong,zhong}. Those frameworks are broader in plant evolution, online inference, or sensor behavior. Our object is instead a fixed-horizon finite multi-class separation task with a symmetric per-record deletion budget. We therefore do not claim the first diagnosability criterion under observation loss; the contribution is the particular local proof format and selected-coordinate preservation argument for this finite contract.
ledger_relevance: Foundational language/observer formulation of diagnosability for discrete-event systems.
ledger_delta_or_limit: Broader diagnosis semantics are prior work; this manuscript claims only a finite fixed-horizon certificate and selected-coordinate preservation result for its explicit deletion contract.
